Realise the atoms of a product

Source: R/product-class.R
product_atoms.Rd

The cross product of the component leaftables: one row per tuple of component atoms, with each axis's key column named by product_keys() and its frame columns prefixed "<axis>.".

product_atoms(x, limit = 1e+06)

Arguments

x

A ScaleProduct.

limit

Maximum number of rows to build. Exceeding it is an error that reports the size, rather than a very long wait.

Value

A data.frame with product_size(x)$total rows.

Details

This is guarded on purpose. An hourly calendar crossed with NUTS3 is ~12.9M rows; the whole point of a product is that its atoms exist implicitly, and conversion never needs them realised (see recast_scale()). Ask for them only when you actually want the grid.

Examples

p <- scale_product(a = scale_example(), b = scale_example2())
head(product_atoms(p))
#>   unit a.sector a.class a.group period b.era
#> 1   U1        P      G1      G1     p1    E1
#> 2   U2        P      G1      G1     p1    E1
#> 3   U3        P      G2      GB     p1    E1
#> 4   U4        P      G2      GB     p1    E1
#> 5   U5        S      S1      GB     p1    E1
#> 6   U6        S      S1      GC     p1    E1
